articles.title: Leader: The enemy dares not venture beyond Arabian Sea — and soon will be driven from there
articles.body:
Leader: The enemy dares not venture beyond Arabian Sea — and soon will be driven from there
TEHRAN – Leader of the Islamic Revolution Ayatollah Seyyed Mojtaba Khamenei issued a message on Monday saying that due to the painful blows that the enemy has suffered at the hands of Iranian armed forces and the guardians of the Strait of Hormuz, it has sought refuge in the Arabian Sea and it will soon be expelled from there.
The following is the full text of the Leader's message issued on the occasion of Sacred Defense Week and the martyrdom anniversary of Lebanese Hezbollah chief Sayyid Hassan Nasrallah:
In the Name of God, the Compassionate, the Merciful
“And verily We sent Moses with Our signs, [saying], ‘Bring your people out from darkness into light and remind them of the Days of Allah’” (Quran 14:5).
The opening days of the month of Mehr are a reminder of the “Days of God” (Ayyam Allah) and that monumental, enduring phenomenon: the eight-year valiant defense of the Iranian nation in the First Imposed War. During those days, the warm radiance of the Revolutionary sun throughout the entire expanse of Iran radiated a gratifying sense of national solidarity and devotion to the ideals and ethos of revolutionary Islam, melting away the ice of both classical colonialism and neo-colonialism and hegemony.
At that time, some Iranians still remembered the hostility of the colonial powers, the events surrounding the nationalization of the oil industry, and the US-backed coup d'état of more than two decades earlier. Others had heard accounts of it, while many had experienced first-hand the brutal reality of what foreign domination over our nation's affairs wrought upon the country. The days preceding that era were dark and bleak, when ambassadors of the Arrogant Powers would dictate their demands and prohibitions to the Shah of Iran, and he would execute those demands – either willingly or reluctantly – until the magnificent Revolution of the Iranian nation, led by the late Imam Khomeini (RA), ripped that order apart. Due to the Revolution, those dark days gave way to the luminous era of the establishment of the Islamic Republic of Iran.
This development was deeply intolerable to the hegemonic powers whose greedy eyes were focused on the wealth of this land. For years, they had inflicted all kinds of atrocities upon Iran’s people to claim those resources for themselves. So, from that moment on, they devoted all their efforts to reversing the roaring surge of the revolutionary nation to go back to its former course. The First Imposed War was their most significant undertaking during the first decade of the blessed existence of the Islamic Republic.
From inside the heart of the flames of that war - which had been ignited by the Ba'ath party that was hostile toward their people, under the delusion of a conflict that would only take days and be a victory requiring little effort – the Islamic system rose like a phoenix, more vigorous and stronger than before, and with a more resounding voice and loftier flight. This became an enduring hallmark of the Islamic system in the subsequent events that were orchestrated by its enemies.
Those days when the enemy of this nation had imposed its puppets upon the people and enforced a new form of colonialism were, due to the blessing of the Revolution and the raising of the banner of Islam and jihad in the midst of the Imposed War, transformed into days of glory. Today, even 38 years after the end of that war, when we examine its events in close detail and listen to the truthful accounts of those who survived it, figures of exemplary stature emerge like brilliant stars in the firmament of our nation’s history. Each one is a model from whom lessons in worship, courage, resistance, morality, and humanity can be learned.
Those early days at the onset of the attacks by the agents of the hegemonic system, our country had inherited nothing from the Taghut (Pahlavi) regime to defend itself against a barrage of threats. But those days have now – due to the blessing of upholding the Truth and through divine assistance – given way to days in which the aggressive hegemonic powers themselves, and not merely their proxies, seek shelter from the attacks of Islam’s soldiers and plead for an end to the war.
Those days to which they long to return our country were days of backwardness, humiliation, dependency, and a tarnishing of Iran’s reputation in the Islamic world. In contrast, the days we live in today are overflowing with progress, dignity, independence, and an elevated level of reputability in the Islamic world and indeed across the globe. Today, there are those who regard us as the world's fourth superpower. Of course, they say this based on worldly calculations. But according to divine calculations, a country that knows itself to be devoted to the pure Household of the Prophet (PBUH), whose people are predominantly attached to those exalted figures, and who have no fear of upholding the Truth, is the world’s foremost power.
In those days, the two seas to the south of Iran were the theater of operations for enemy forces. But today, because of the painful blows the enemy has suffered at the hands of our valiant fighters and the guardians of the Strait of Hormuz, they dare not advance beyond the Arabian Sea. Whenever they have risked doing so, they themselves have suffered. And it won’t be long before the Arabian Sea rids itself of their presence too.
There was a time when the hegemonic powers, through psychological warfare and by creating an atmosphere of fear, emptied the streets of the capital and staged a coup against this nation’s struggle for independence. After that, they plundered the wealth of this country for 25 years. But now for seven months, our compatriots have adorned the public squares and streets throughout the country with their enthusiastic, responsible presence, warming the hearts of those fighting for Islam while striking fear into the enemy.
Over 30 million Iranians have declared their willingness to sacrifice their lives. And when they were called upon to reconfirm their readiness as part of a certain organizational effort, more than 500,000 people filled the requested capacity within the first 100 minutes alone. Today, there are various declarations of readiness throughout Islamic Iran, particularly for armed participation, creating an arena in which our people will gain honor and their enemy disgrace. There were days when the heroic spirit of the people of this land was recognized through its men. But today, we live in times where women surpass men in several arenas with their courageous presence.
There were days when the enemy sought to continuously erode the social bedrock of the system. But today, people from all walks of life, despite their obvious differences, stand resolutely in defending their righteous positions, including their determination to safeguard the bountiful Strait of Hormuz.
This comparison between the days of the past and the present can be further expanded upon, but in one word, I, as a servant of the dear people of Iran, declare that those bygone days to which our enemy longs to return have passed and will never be repeated. Of course, I must recall with sorrow and grief that these days, the absence of the Great Khomeini and the illustrious Martyr Khamenei (may God elevate their noble stations) is felt deeply. The country’s present dignity owes a great debt to their leadership. Nonetheless, by virtue of the invaluable treasure of their deeds and radiant, guiding words left behind for their followers, the coming days will be vastly more glorious than the present. For the phoenix that arose from the ashes of the First Imposed War has now, under the pressure of enemy hostilities and particularly the two recent Imposed Wars, grown so majestic that the shadow of its flight now extends over the lands of the enemy as well.
On this occasion of the second anniversary of the martyrdom of the heroic commander of the Arab world and the great symbol of the Resistance Front, the exalted martyr, His Eminence Sayyid Hassan Nasrallah (may God sanctify his pure soul), it’s very fitting to remember him. He was a sincere well-wisher for his people and his faith. His sincere and eloquent sermons, together with his courageous actions, strengthened the hearts of his people and, indeed, the hearts of the free people of the world. He elevated the name of Lebanon, which is a small country that for years had served as a backyard for foreign powers, to greatness. Victory and triumph were his constant companions. Without a doubt, no figure - after the prophets and their successors - has ever arisen of his stature in that ancient land throughout the entire history of the Levant.
Today, his glorious banner is in the hands of His Eminence Sheikh Naim Qassem (may God protect him), who courageously leads the resolute, Ashura-inspired ranks of Hezbollah, who continue his path.
These current days in Lebanon – even now before the judgment of history – are outstanding, glorious days for its people and all fighters of the Resistance. They’re days that bring humiliation and ultimate disgrace upon those who pin their hopes on the false promises of the hegemonic powers and the people’s ill-wishers when facing the Zionist enemy. Unlike the martyred Sayyid of the Resistance, Sayyid Hashem Safieddine, and the current fighters of the Resistance – who will continue to shine like radiant stars throughout time and will guide those who seek the way when lost in bewilderment – those powers will be swiftly buried and forgotten at the very first turn of history's pages. Whenever they are recalled in the future, they will only be reminders of malice, folly, and perhaps even betrayal.
In conclusion, I am hopeful that, with the continued bestowal of divine grace and the special prayers of our Master (Imam Mahdi) (may God hasten his noble reappearance and may our souls be sacrificed for him), the Iranian nation and all the allies of the Resistance will encounter only victory, triumph, and glory, while their enemies will only suffer defeat and humiliation, by God’s grace and through His bounty.

articles.title: Top NATO commander urges states to condemn Russian acts of sabotage
articles.body:
Top NATO commander urges states to condemn Russian acts of sabotage
BRUSSELS, Sept 28 - NATO Supreme Allied Commander Europe Alexus Grynkewich said on Monday that the best way for European countries to respond to Russian sabotage and other destabilising acts was to state when Moscow was to blame and strengthen their support for Ukraine.
Acts of sabotage, cyberattacks, drone sightings and other so-called hybrid attacks attributed to Russia have multiplied in the past months in many European countries and include a drone attack in Leipzig and a Russian strike on a train in Ukraine near the Polish border earlier this month.
"Bringing that attribution out publicly will let state sponsors know that we understand what they're doing and that increases costs on them," he told EU lawmakers in a Parliament committee on Monday.
"They will realise that their networks are ineffective and that they have to modify their behaviour and that, in and of itself, has some deterrent effect," he added.
Russian activity in Europe aims at breaking allies' will in continuing to support Kyiv, he said.
The supreme commander added that NATO initiatives such as the Eastern Sentry mission launched on September 11 and comprising assets from allies such as Denmark, France, Britain, Germany have already had an effect on the ground.
"The Russians have been much more careful to avoid coming across the border with drones in the Baltics or into Poland since we implemented Eastern Sentry," he said. REUTERS

articles.title: US envoy says Trump asked Xi about buying American weapons
articles.body:
TAIPEI (Taiwan News) — US Ambassador to China David Perdue said President Donald Trump once asked Chinese leader Xi Jinping whether China wanted to buy American weapons while discussing Washington’s arms sales to Taiwan, the Financial Times reported Monday.
Perdue made the disclosure when asked about reports that Trump had delayed a proposed NT$439 billion (US$14 billion) arms package for Taiwan to avoid upsetting Xi. Perdue said Trump had noted that the US sells weapons to countries around the world and “at one point” asked Xi whether China wanted to buy some.
Perdue did not say when Trump made the remark or provide further details. The White House also did not say how Xi responded.
A US official told the Financial Times that Washington had no plans to sell weapons to China. The State Department subsequently said US law prohibits such sales and that there was no offer or plan to provide weapons to Beijing.
The Trump administration has also raised concerns about Beijing providing Iran with dual-use technology that could have military applications, per ABC News.
Perdue rejected suggestions that the status of the Taiwan package reflected an effort to avoid harming relations with Beijing. He said US policy toward Taiwan had not changed and discussions over the proposed sale were continuing.
Taiwan Representative to the US Alexander Yui (俞大㵢) said the US remains Taiwan’s main weapons supplier. He said Taiwan hoped to receive the proposed package “as soon as possible.”

articles.title: Besomar 1100 Reconnaissance UAV and Besomar 3210 FV Mapping System Unveiled in Ukraine
articles.body:
The Ukrainian company Besomar develops drones with support from the Brave1 grant program and the European Cluster for Drone Innovation (ECDI).
The company Besomar reported this to Militarnyi.
The military line is represented by the Besomar 1100 reconnaissance unmanned aerial vehicle.
Structurally, the UAV is built according to a classic aircraft configuration with a straight, high-mounted wing and a V-shaped tail. Winglets are mounted at the wing tips. A propeller is located in the tail section, and an optoelectronic surveillance system mounted in a gyro-stabilized gimbal is installed beneath the nose of the fuselage.
The UAV is designed for aerial reconnaissance and long-endurance surveillance. The system is already being delivered to Ukrainian units for combat use.
The Besomar 1100 has a range of up to 100 km and a flight duration of up to 4 hours. The UAV has a cruising speed of 90–100 km/h, a maximum speed of up to 160 km/h, and is capable of operating at altitudes of up to 5,500 meters. Special technical solutions have been implemented in the system to counter electronic warfare (EW) measures.
At the same time, the company is expanding into the civilian sector by developing the Besomar 3210 FV system for aerial photography, mapping, and creating digital terrain models.
The project is being implemented jointly with Farsight Vision as part of the ECDI Civil Drones Innovative Programme. The joint development is intended for monitoring civilian and critical infrastructure, as well as spatial analysis.
In August, during field tests in Ukraine, specialists tested the full cycle — from executing the flight mission and collecting aerial imagery to its subsequent software processing.
During the test photography mission, the drone covered approximately 2.9 km² of territory, and the resulting aerial images were used to create an orthophoto map.
The Besomar 3210 FV has a takeoff weight of 9.7 kg with a payload capacity of up to 1 kg. The drone is capable of covering a route of up to 200 km with a range of up to 60 km and remaining airborne for over 3 hours. The civilian model’s cruising speed is 80–90 km/h, and its maximum speed reaches 160 km/h. Launch is performed via a catapult, and landing is carried out automatically.
The drone is integrated into the unified Besomar ecosystem, operates with its own ground control station, and is capable of navigating using beacons without relying on GPS systems.

articles.title: Indian imports of Russian crude oil to decline further amid lower exports, Chinese competition
articles.body:
Tourists watch marine life, with the MT Desert Kite oil tanker carrying Russian oil in the background (Photo: Reuters).
NEW DELHI: Indian refiners expect Russian oil supplies to decline further in October and November, owing to lower exports and stiff competition from China, forcing the country to buy costlier alternatives for the rest of the year.People familiar with procurement plans told Reuters that some Indian refiners would not receive adequate Russian supplies in October and November."Demand from China has been really high. They were willing to book cargoes in advance and to pay firmer prices compared to Indian refiners," a source involved in the sale of Russian crude said.According to analytics firm Kpler, Russian oil arrivals in India are set to drop to around 1.75 million barrels per day in September, the lowest level since April.Trade data showed that arrivals had already fallen 16.5 per cent to about 2.1 million bpd in August from July, although Russia remained India's main supplier, ahead of the UAE and Venezuela.Overall availability of Russian exports has reportedly shrunk, particularly from the Black Sea port of Novorossiysk, where shipments have roughly halved as repeated drone attacks have suspended loadings.India has been the top buyer of seaborne Russian Urals crude since 2022, when Moscow diverted its energy flows away from Europe at deep discounts.
In recent months, however, China, the world's top crude importer, has stepped up its purchases as Middle Eastern supplies tightened because of the Iran war.
Alternatives
Traders told Reuters that refiners have turned to pricier replacement barrels, seeking UAE Murban, a close substitute for Russia's Urals grade, while also buying Iraqi Basrah and Angolan cargoes.
Shipping dynamics have helped redirect flows to China.Seasonal navigation along the Arctic Northern Sea Route (NSR) offers a secure and cost-effective channel for Russian crude exports to China, whereas shipments to India via the Red Sea face heightened security risks linked to the conflict involving Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis."It's not so much about the price as ensuring the cargo actually reaches its destination," another trader told Reuters, adding that freight costs via the Arctic route to China are now broadly comparable with shipments through the Suez Canal.

articles.title: Former Shin Bet chief threatens defamation suit against Netanyahu, demands schedule disclosure
articles.body:
Former Shin Bet (Israel Security Agency) chief Ronen Bar announced on Monday evening that he intends to file a defamation lawsuit against Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, while demanding the release of testimonies and documents related to information provided to the prime minister before October 7.
Bar is also demanding the disclosure of Netanyahu's schedule of meetings with the defense establishment and foreign officials. He said he intends to summon members of the prime minister's office and his aides to testify, claiming they assisted and continue to assist Netanyahu in a "manipulative campaign."
A statement on behalf of Bar said: "Prime Minister Netanyahu launched an unrestrained incitement campaign against the former Shin Bet chief, one that has no basis in reality."
According to Bar, after Netanyahu refused for three years to acknowledge his responsibility and prevented the public from receiving a state commission of inquiry, he began releasing portions of documents "in a manipulative manner and detached from their true context."
The statement further claimed that as testimonies begin to emerge regarding warnings Netanyahu received before the October 7 massacre, he is "attempting to divert the fire away from himself" by accusing those who warned him in real time.
Bar claims he warned PM of impending disaster before October 7
According to Bar, during his tenure as Shin Bet chief, he warned the prime minister of an "impending disaster" in an unprecedented manner, but Netanyahu allegedly ignored those warnings, as well as recommendations to restore deterrence and strengthen the border.
"Until now, Ronen Bar believed it was right to wait for the establishment of the commission to which the public and the bereaved families are entitled. However, the string of lies cannot be allowed to continue," his statement said.
"Lies, distortion of facts, manipulation of protocols, and the dissemination of misleading information to the public, this is what the prime minister is doing as the extent of the warnings he received before the October 7 massacre is beginning to become clear."
Following the statement, Bar instructed his lawyers to file a defamation lawsuit against Netanyahu and summon for testimony anyone who, according to him, "distorted, falsified documents, and spread false and defamatory information" against him.
He also called on the prime minister to immediately release all documents so that the public can, in his words, "be exposed to the full truth, without manipulation."
The statement added that the defamation lawsuit and the disclosure of information resulting from it are also important "to protect the memory of the fallen, the honor of Shin Bet personnel who have been fighting in the shadows for three years, and the truth," which Bar claims the prime minister is attempting to distort through a campaign of incitement against the heads of the security establishment.
Bar concluded his statement by saying: "Victory is achieved through a preemptive attack against the enemy outside, not against the security forces at home."
Earlier on Monday, Netanyahu denied a report by The Wall Street Journal, citing senior officials in an Arab government, that then Egyptian intelligence chief Abbas Kamel warned him in a phone call about an impending attack from the Gaza Strip days before the October 7 massacre.
Netanyahu also attacked Bar, saying: "He was aware of a real danger on the night of October 7, and did not update me."
A statement published on Netanyahu's X/Twitter account said that "no Israeli intelligence official passed on an Egyptian warning to the prime minister," and that the prime minister's office had instructed lawyers to file a defamation lawsuit on this issue as well.
In his response, Netanyahu referred to The Wall Street Journal report that then Egyptian General Intelligence Service chief Abbas Kamel called him in early October 2023, days before the October 7 massacre, and delivered a third warning regarding signs of an impending attack from the Gaza Strip.
"In the months before October 7, I did not meet or speak with Abbas Kamel, who was then head of Egypt's General Intelligence Service," Netanyahu's denial statement said.
"The prime minister never meets or speaks with the intelligence chief of a foreign country without their Israeli counterparts being present."
According to Netanyahu, "in recent weeks, the left-wing media has been conducting a malicious and false campaign intended to place all of Ronen Bar's failures and crimes before October 7 on Prime Minister Netanyahu, while on the night of October 7, Shin Bet chief Ronen Bar held many conversations with then IDF Chief of Staff Herzi Halevi and then Military Intelligence chief Aharon Haliva, in which they discussed all the warning signs."
Netanyahu claimed that "despite this, Ronen Bar decided not to call and update the prime minister, not to warn the civilian security squads and IDF forces in the field, not to evacuate the Nova festival, and only send a small Tequila team, proving that he knew of a real danger."
Netanyahu says foreign actors are behind "blood libels"
After attacking Ronen Bar, Netanyahu turned his criticism toward "foreign and hostile actors," claiming they were behind "false blood libels."
"Behind these false blood libels are also foreign countries, including Arab countries, with the aim of toppling Netanyahu's right-wing government and replacing it with a government of left-wing parties and Arab parties led by Eisenkot, Yair Golan, and Liberman that will withdraw from Gaza, Lebanon, Syria, and Judea and Samaria, and establish a Palestinian state."
According to the Wall Street Journal report, citing senior officials in an Arab government, then Egyptian intelligence chief Abbas Kamel called Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in early October 2023, days before the October 7 massacre, and delivered a third warning regarding signs of an impending attack from the Gaza Strip.
According to the newspaper, the direct conversation between Kamel and Netanyahu had not previously been made public and was one of several early warnings received by Netanyahu and other senior Israeli officials before the attack.

articles.title: India’s Sheikh Hasina Dilemma
articles.body:
The mass street uprising that overthrew Bangladesh’s long-serving prime minister, Sheikh Hasina, in August 2024 did more than just reset the politics of a nation. It completely broke the security architecture of eastern South Asia. For 15 years, India’s foreign policy in its immediate neighborhood relied on a single, unwavering rule: keep Hasina stable, and India’s eastern border remains secure.
Today, that strategy has brought about a major crisis. Hasina is living in exile on Indian soil, while a newly elected government led by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman and the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) runs Dhaka. A Bangladeshi court has convicted Hasina in absentia for crimes against humanity and sentenced her to death, leading Dhaka to officially demand her extradition.
This situation creates a complex challenge for New Delhi, known as the “Hasina dilemma.” It is a problem that cannot be solved simply by picking a side. Instead, it serves as a masterclass in how personal diplomacy can trap a major power, leaving India with difficult arguments to balance as it navigates this regional crisis.
India’s dilemma is rooted in a fundamental rule of global statecraft: credibility. For over a decade, Hasina risked her own domestic popularity to fulfil India’s core national security demands. Her government cracked down heavily on anti-India insurgent groups that used to hide in Bangladesh, arresting their leaders and handing them over to New Delhi. She opened up crucial transit routes, allowing Indian cargo ships and trucks to cut through Bangladesh to reach India’s landlocked northeastern states.
If India gives in to Dhaka’s demands and extradites Hasina to face a death sentence, it sends a dangerous signal to other neighbors like Bhutan, Nepal, and Sri Lanka: India will abandon its closest partners if the political winds change.
However, keeping Hasina protected inside India comes at an equally high cost. It provides permanent fuel for anti-India sentiment within Bangladesh’s civil society. The longer India acts as her shield, the easier it is for the BNP government to label New Delhi as an enemy of Bangladesh’s democracy. This anger puts India’s vital trade links and transit corridors at immediate risk of being shut down by a hostile public.
The strain on the relationship is no longer just quiet, back-channel friction; it has broken out into visible diplomatic boycotts. Rahman’s recent decision to skip the high-profile BRICS Summit hosted by India in New Delhi served as a clear example of this shift.
Dhaka viewed the invitation to the summit – extended to Rahman as the chair of a regional group (BIMSTEC) rather than as a direct, standalone invite to the premier – as a deliberate diplomatic snub by India. In retaliation, Rahman refused to travel to New Delhi altogether.
Instead, Rahman deliberately focused his diplomatic efforts elsewhere: a high-profile trip to the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA), where he held a sideline meeting with the Pakistani leadership. At the same time, Rahman’s administration deepened talks with Beijing over major infrastructure loans.
By refusing a standalone visit to New Delhi, Rahman is sending a clear message: The days of Bangladesh automatically aligning with India’s foreign policy goals are over. Dhaka is demonstrating that it is fully willing to use its strategic geography to balance India’s influence, using closer ties with Islamabad and Beijing as leverage to show that Bangladesh is no longer dependent on New Delhi’s approval.
The Hasina Dilemma serves as a systemic warning to foreign policy planners worldwide: never mistake a single political leader for an entire country.
For 15 years, India’s Ministry of External Affairs operated under the assumption that keeping Hasina happy was equivalent to keeping Bangladesh stable. New Delhi looked the other way during consecutive, highly controversial Bangladeshi elections, prioritizing immediate border security over the growing domestic anger building up against her regime.
By tying its national interests so tightly to one person, India failed to build deep institutional relationships with Bangladesh’s opposition parties, its student movements, and its wider civil society.
Now that Hasina has fallen, India faces a significant penalty for this policy. The new leadership in Dhaka views almost every regular, technical bilateral issue – from regular border management to daily electricity grid sharing – through a lens of deep suspicion. Because India did not engage with the broader political spectrum when it had the chance, it must now build diplomatic capital from scratch with a suspicious administration, all while dealing with the political liability of hosting the former leader.
The relationship between India and Bangladesh cannot remain frozen in this defensive stance forever. Bangladesh relies heavily on India for daily essential food imports, medical tourism, and electricity. Conversely, India requires a cooperative Dhaka to ensure its northeastern states do not become cut off or vulnerable to security threats.
Signs of a realistic compromise are slowly beginning to show. Recognizing the danger of a complete breakdown in relations, India’s diplomats have adopted a quiet, disciplined approach, consistently stating their desire for a “constructive and forward-looking relations” with the new government. This back-channel diplomacy has successfully defused the initial freeze, setting up an official state visit for Rahman to New Delhi in late November or early December 2026.
To make this upcoming visit a success and move past the crisis, both nations must cooperate on a silent, two-part strategy.
First, find a third country willing to provide permanent asylum to Sheikh Hasina. India must quietly work to relocate Hasina to a secure country outside South Asia, such as in the Middle East or parts of Europe. This move would allow Dhaka to claim a political victory to its domestic voters while sparing India the immense loss of face that would come from direct extradition.
Second, India and Bangladesh must shift to transactional institutionalism. Both capitals must agree to treat critical issues – like the upcoming December 2026 Ganga Water Sharing Treaty deadline – as technical, non-negotiable economic necessities rather than emotional political weapons.
The Hasina Dilemma proves that in modern geopolitics, yesterday’s absolute stability can easily become tomorrow’s greatest strategic trap. Bangladesh-India relations will likely never return to the close, personal alliance of the past decade. The relationship has permanently shifted into a cooler, more transactional reality.
Even so, if both New Delhi and Dhaka can successfully separate their internal political speeches from their shared geographic realities, they can prevent the presence of a single deposed leader from turning a temporary diplomatic crisis into a long-term regional disaster.

articles.title: Ukraine trains military orphans to ‘replace fallen fathers’ – WaPo
articles.body:
Ukraine trains military orphans to ‘replace fallen fathers’ – WaPo
The Ukrainian government has set up five boarding schools for children whose parents were killed, went missing, or were left disabled in the conflict with Russia, preparing them for careers in the country’s military service, The Washington Post has reported.
The newspaper gained access to one of the institutions for a report published on Monday, describing the two-year boarding schools as “part grief counseling and part boot camp,” effectively sealing the fate of the vulnerable children.
“[The] school puts them into a funnel toward the Ukrainian security services that are desperate for recruits, along with hundreds of other cadets at new government academies devoted to the still-young children of fallen fighters,” the article reads.
The children are also being prepared for “university entrance exams in their second year” and are required to complete a degree even if they choose to enter service. School staff insisted that “no pressure” be put on the cadets to pursue such careers, the Post noted.
The Ukrainian military needs some 30,000 fresh recruits per month just to maintain its current force size, the Post noted, citing Ukrainian officials. “Officially, Ukraine reports that about 55,000 have been killed in the war and about 114,000 are missing. But aid providers say those figures don’t begin to reflect the number of children who have lost at least one parent,” the article reads.
Independent casualty estimates, however, differ drastically from the official Ukrainian figures, with the US-based Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS) estimating that Ukrainian forces have suffered between 525,000 and 625,000 casualties, including those killed, wounded, and missing.
Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk recently said that the Ukrainian military was suffering 27,000 casualties a month.
Kiev has long struggled to replenish its ranks through forced conscription, with its mobilization effort growing increasingly chaotic and violent over the course of the conflict.
The mobilization campaign, dubbed ‘busification,’ has often involved draft officers ambushing military-age men on the streets, at workplaces, and outside their homes, using violence against those resisting or attempting to flee. The draft has sparked several protests and riots across the country, which the authorities have dismissed as “helping the enemy.”
The involvement of children in paramilitary training has been on the rise in Ukraine since the 2014 Western-backed Euromaidan coup, with the process accelerating further in the wake of the full-blown conflict with Russia. The idea of lowering age thresholds for such training and, potentially, for active service has been repeatedly floated by various public figures. Moreover, boot camps for children have frequently been set up by openly neo-Nazi groups, with basic training going hand in hand with hateful indoctrination at such facilities.

articles.title: Nvidia’s Answer to Rogue Agents Is an Open-Source AI Security System
articles.body:
Amidst ongoing reports of AI agents wreaking havoc on online infrastructure, chipmaker Nvidia is rallying tech companies to use its new open-source tool for AI security.
Over the last few months, frontier AI labs have disclosed multiple incidents in which AI agents have hacked into other companies or, in more recent examples, probed official US and Australian government websites. While Nvidia has already taken a leading role in rallying the AI industry around open source security, it’s now introducing one new software security platform and making an agentic AI sandbox more broadly available.
OpenShell, one of the Nvidia’s recently launched security sandboxes for AI agents, is now entering general release for all users. OpenShell was first announced at Nvidia’s annual GTC Conference in March; it’s a framework for containing agents as they carry out tasks and isolating their activity in the operating system kernel, the foundational program that has access to virtually all parts of a computer system in order to coordinate hardware and software.
Nvidia’s launch materials indicate that it has AI safety and security collaborations with dozens of other tech companies, including Anthropic, Cisco, CoreWeave, CrowdStrike, Dell Technologies, Hugging Face, JPMorganChase, Mistral, Microsoft, and Palantir. Nvidia says SpaceXAI is using the Open Agent Safety Platform for its Cursor agents and Grok models. The company also says Anthropic and Nvidia are “building security into Claude Managed Agents.” Salesforce, Scale AI, and SAP are all confirmed to be integrating OpenShell to some degree. However, it is unclear whether OpenShell has been adopted by Nvidia’s full list of partners, or whether Nvidia is gesturing broadly.
One notable name is missing entirely from Nvidia’s list: OpenAI. Both companies indicated that OpenAI is a part of Nvidia’s OpenShell effort, though both declined to comment directly on why the AI lab was excluded from the announcement.
Security engineers and AI safety experts have considered the need to isolate and monitor agentic AI since well before the recent revelations of rogue agent hacking. Nvidia’s own OpenShell announcement in March noted that the framework would add “privacy and security controls to make self-evolving, autonomous AI agents, or claws, more trustworthy, scalable and accessible,” months before OpenAI disclosed that its AI agents had hacked the open source AI company Hugging Face. (Nvidia agreed to acquire Hugging Face earlier this month for $12.9 billion.)
The chip giant has also developed a new software platform called Sentry, an isolated security domain for chips that’s supposed to continuously monitor long-running AI agents. While Sentry is technically a software tool, it’s meant to be implemented on Bluefield, Nvidia’s line of programmable data processing units (DPUs). The idea is that in addition to the restrictions imposed by OpenShell, Sentry can act as a separate, independent mechanism that can “quarantine agents that attempt to move outside their boundaries.”
Sentry is another way for Nvidia customers and open-source users to actually implement security policies through OpenShell, says Justin Boitano, Nvidia’s vice president and general manager of enterprise computing. While traditional sandboxes are built for “application-level isolation,” people now want to run fleets of agents, which demands a “collective policy across all of those agents,” he says.
“Agents are very creative at finding ways to achieve the goals that they’re given,” Boitano says. “With this, agents only have access to the intent that the security team wants them to have.”
Boitano adds that Nvidia is working with both Arm and Intel to create a version of Sentry that works on the x86 chip architecture. “Once it runs on those instruction-set architectures, it can run on any architecture,” he says.
Nvidia is positioning all of this as part of a new open-source framework called the Open Agent Safety Platform, which now encompasses OpenShell and Sentry as well.
In July Nvidia launched an industry-wide AI safety coalition that now comprises more than 120 companies. The coalition’s stated goal was to reduce AI risks, particularly through a program called the Shared AI Findings Exchange (SAFE). Last month, Boitano said that SAFE was designed to be “governed independently, with no single company or industry segment controlling its findings.”
But one company keeps appearing at the center of these industry-wide, open-source AI initiatives, and that company is Nvidia. The world’s most valuable company, on which most of the tech industry depends on for the most performant chips, appears to be positioning itself to deepen its influence and set standards at varying levels of the AI technology stack, from silicon to security software.
Though efforts to contain and control agents are already in progress throughout the industry, recent rogue agent behavior suggests a need to raise awareness about long-standing, core security practices—even, apparently, within trillion-dollar frontier labs. Some experts say that this also gets to the heart of the question about what it really means for an autonomous piece of software to “go rogue.”
“Anything that makes it easy for companies to deploy agents in a way that has more guardrails and more safety should be applauded,” says longtime security engineer and researcher Niels Provos, speaking generally about tools geared toward containing and monitoring agents. Provos himself launched an open source framework in February focused on these issues. “If nothing else, these types of tools help to dispel the myth that agents can’t be controlled.”

articles.title: Space Force Interested in Commercial Antennas to Control Satellites
articles.body:
The Space Force is starting a new competition to bolster its network of antennas that track and manage Pentagon and other U.S. government satellites—and this time, acquisition officials are open to leasing commercial systems or even paying for commercial antennas as a service.
In a Sept. 24 notice, the Space Force and the Missile Defense Agency announced they are resetting the Satellite Communications Augmentation Resource program with a “Commercial Solutions Opening.” Instead of providing a list of detailed requirements, these openings define “areas of interest,” inviting vendors to pitch ideas based on commercially available technology.
The SCAR program is the Space Force’s effort to “revitalize” its Cold War-era Satellite Control Network, a collection of 19 antennas dispersed around the globe that track and maneuver satellites and collect data about their health and status. The service awarded and later canceled a $1.4 billion contract for Blue Halo, now part of AeroVironment, to build and deliver 12 multibeam, phased-array antennas for SCAR.
After cancelling that deal in March, officials explained they wanted to leverage commercial technology rather than acquire a bespoke, Space Force-centric design. This latest announcement offers more details on the approch, detailing three “areas of interest” for the SCAR program:
- A government-owned, contractor-operated model using commercial systems
- Long-term, exclusive government leases of commercially owned and operated systems
- “Antenna as a Service” giving the government access to commercial systems that could also be used by other customers
Each area of interest has benefits and drawbacks, the announcement states. Government-owned often means “bespoke technical solutions, Government-led maintenance,” and limited funding, officials wrote. Leasing or antenna-as-a-service carries security concerns, including “cyber risks that must be mitigated, such as multi-tenant data leakage, scheduling conflicts, and software interoperability bottlenecks.”
But the announcement lays out why Space Force leaders are eager to avoid rerunning the usual acquisition playbook.
“Space operations demand global, high-frequency satellite passes, yet owning and operating a globally distributed physical network is financially burdensome,” the announcement states. “Shifting to commercial ‘shared’ networks alleviates the need to establish dozens of Government-owned sites or dedicated leases.”
The current Satellite Control Network antennas can maintain contact with only one satellite at a time and not for very long. The network’s capacity is under strain as the Pentagon and other government agencies put up more and more spacecraft. According to a 2023 Government Accountability Office report, utilization rates have already been higher than the industry standard for the past decade, and Space Force leaders are expecting the number of satellites on orbit to greatly expand in the coming years.
Companies interested in SCAR have until Oct. 15 to submit white papers. The program office will then select one or more to move to a second phase of consideration.

articles.title: Le Pen scores ‘historic victory’ in French Senate vote
articles.body:
Le Pen scores ‘historic victory’ in French Senate vote
Marine Le Pen’s right-wing National Rally (RN) and an allied party have won enough seats in the French Senate to form a group for the first time. The breakthrough comes months before a presidential election in which polls currently put Le Pen in the lead. 
RN and the Union of the Right for the Republic (UDR) will together hold at least 15 seats in the 348-seat upper house following Sunday’s vote. A group requires a minimum of ten members and gives its lawmakers a greater role in Senate committees, where legislation is examined. 
“This is a historic victory, and a major milestone with the formation for the first time of a group in the Senate,” Le Pen wrote on X. She said the result showed the party gaining support across France and that its senators would carry the concerns of local communities into the presidential campaign.
Despite RN’s latest gains, the Senate will remain controlled by the conservative Republicans and their centrist allies. 
RN president Jordan Bardella has nevertheless called the result a sign of the party’s momentum ahead of what he described as “the mother of all battles,” referring to the upcoming presidential election.
In July, the Paris Court of Appeals reduced Le Pen’s five-year ban on holding elected office over a misused funds conviction, clearing her to run in the 2027 race to replace Emmanuel Macron who will be leaving office after serving two terms. 
A Toluna Harris Interactive poll published on Monday has placed Le Pen as the frontrunner at 35-36% in the first round and projected that she would defeat both left-wing France Unbowed leader Jean-Luc Melenchon and centrist former Prime Minister Edouard Philippe in hypothetical runoffs. 
The RN breakthrough has drawn a hostile response from rival factions, including from Socialist Senate group leader Patrick Kanner, who said his party would work to contain the “chamber of horrors” entering the Senate. 
Le Pen accused Kanner of “dishonoring himself” and insulting both the newly elected senators and the local officials who voted for them. 
The prospect of Le Pen replacing Macron raised particular concerns among the Western backers of Ukraine. The Telegraph reported in August that officials fear her election could disrupt the French-led effort to coordinate military and financial support for Kiev, as well as plans to deploy Western troops there after a ceasefire. 
RN has long challenged Macron’s approach to the Ukraine conflict, opposing open-ended funding for Kiev and steps it says risk a direct confrontation with Russia. Le Pen has repeatedly stressed that the conflict needs a diplomatic solution and has called for normalizing relations with Moscow.

articles.title: US to grant sanctions waiver for flights between Iran and Iraq's Najaf, source says
articles.body:
US to grant sanctions waiver for flights between Iran and Iraq's Najaf, source says
Sept 28 - US President Donald Trump's administration was set to grant a limited waiver to its Iran sanctions program on Monday to allow for flights carrying Shi'ite Muslim religious pilgrims between Iran and Iraq, a person with direct knowledge of the matter said.
The source, who is involved in the deliberations, said the US Treasury Department waiver would allow Iraqi Airways to fly back and forth between Iran and the Shi'ite holy city of Najaf in Iraq for one month, with a more permanent waiver potentially following.
Iraq halted flights to and from Iran on Friday, in line with US sanctions.
The source said the move aimed to ease pressure on the Iraqi government of Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi, who has sought to deepen ties with Washington while also balancing a strong relationship with Iraq's influential neighbour, Iran.
Trump's effort to impose a crippling economic blockade on Iran is forcing regional governments to scale back ties with Iran, creating potential backlash against those states, particularly those that balance their ties with both Washington and Tehran.
Zaidi's office over the weekend said that Iraq was seeking an exemption for travel between Iran and Iraq for medical treatment, education and pilgrimage.
An Iraqi official said the Iraqi government was in talks with the US about the Najaf exemption and expected flights between Iran and Najaf to resume within 48 hours.
The US State Department referred questions to the Treasury Department, which did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
In recent days, countries including Turkey, the UAE and Iraq have cancelled direct flights with Iran as a result of US pressure. In response, Iranian officials have threatened to halt regional air travel if Iran's air links continued to be cut.
With Shi'ite religious pilgrims travelling between Iran and Iraq each year to visit key shrine cities, Iraq is perhaps in the most sensitive position.
Najaf, a center for religious study, draws millions of pilgrims a year to the shrine of Imam Ali, the first Shi'ite leader, and the world’s largest and oldest active Islamic cemetery.
The source said that barring flights between the two countries could cause severe backlash against Iraq's government by uniting Shi'ites who follow Iran's supreme leader and those who follow Iraq's Grand Ayatollah Ali al-Sistani, undermining US efforts to reduce Iranian influence in Iraq.
Zaidi has offered to provide safeguards for the flights, including rigorous screening and information sharing as well as ensuring the flights are not used for transfer of weapons, sanctioned individuals or illicit money, the source said. REUTERS

articles.title: Netanyahu asked UAE to cover up prior October 7 knowledge – media
articles.body:
Netanyahu asked UAE to cover up prior October 7 knowledge – media
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu reportedly secretly flew to the UAE to ask President Mohamed bin Zayed to deny that he had warned the Jewish state of a major Hamas threat ahead of the deadly October 7 attack.
Netanyahu has faced growing scrutiny over claims that he had received multiple warnings from regional countries in the run-up to the Hamas-led incursion, which killed around 1,200 people, saw 251 taken hostage, and which led to the Gaza war.
Netanyahu met bin Zayed for about an hour in Abu Dhabi on Sunday to ask the Emirati president to deny the warning claim, AP reported on Monday, citing two people briefed on the trip.
Haaretz first reported earlier this month that Emirati intelligence had alerted Israel’s Shin Bet security service to a possible major Hamas operation, prompting bin Zayed to call Netanyahu about ten days before the assault. The UAE president reportedly warned that the plan could lead to bloodshed and destabilize the region.
Netanyahu reportedly played down the threat, saying he believed Hamas was more likely to act in the occupied West Bank and that Israel was prepared. His office has rejected the Haaretz report as an “absolute lie,” insisting no such call took place.
Egypt reportedly also gave Israel advance warning. The Atlantic reported that then-intelligence chief Abbas Kamel traveled to Israel less than two weeks before the attack to alert officials that Hamas appeared to be preparing a major operation.
The Wall Street Journal reported on Sunday that Cairo had issued at least three warnings, including one to Netanyahu’s office just days before the incursion, and continued contacting Israel until roughly 48 hours before the attack. Netanyahu has denied receiving advance notice from Egypt.
Israeli intelligence had separately obtained a Hamas battle plan known as ‘Jericho Wall’, outlining a cross-border assault, attacks on military positions and hostage-taking. The New York Times later reported that the document closely resembled the October 7 attack, although Israeli officials have disputed how seriously it was taken and whether it was considered an imminent threat.
Former IDF chief of staff Dan Halutz has accused Netanyahu of concealing the warnings, saying the failure was “total, broad, and included everyone,” and that the prime minister bore ultimate responsibility.
Earlier this month, families of Israelis killed or abducted in the attack unveiled a 12-page dossier arguing that it was not simply an intelligence failure, but the result of a long-running policy under successive Netanyahu governments.
The controversy comes ahead of parliamentary elections scheduled for October 27. Netanyahu, who faces a challenge from former IDF chief of staff Gadi Eisenkot, has described the Haaretz report as “politically motivated” and part of the “left’s election campaign.”

articles.title: Miliband distances Britain from Trump’s G20 Putin invite
articles.body:
LIVERPOOL, England — Britain’s chief diplomat said Monday that the U.K. will not ditch its ban on directly engaging with Russian officials after Donald Trump invited Vladimir Putin to the G20 meeting in December.
Speaking in The POLITICO Pub at Labour Party conference, Ed Miliband said it is for the U.S. to “make their own decisions” on inviting the Russian president to the summit in Miami later this year — but stressed the U.K. is unlikely to take the same approach next year.
“We’ve had a long-standing policy not to have direct engagement at my level with the Russians since the invasion of Ukraine. We’re not changing that policy,” Miliband said when asked whether the greater engagement with Moscow is a good thing.
Advertisement
Miliband said the decision is in part about showing solidarity with the Ukrainian people, adding: “Different countries make different decisions on these things.”
The U.K. foreign secretary confirmed Prime Minister Andy Burnham will be at the Miami G20 later this year, but declined to “second guess the decisions” about who’s invited.
Elsewhere in his interview, Miliband acknowledged that disagreements with the Trump administration over the future of the Chagos Islands were discussed when Burnham met Trump at the U.N. General Assembly earlier this month.
“It’s pretty clear, as became apparent from that meeting, that the U.S. administration does not at the moment agree with the arrangement,” Miliband said, adding he and U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio “talk a lot” about the way forward. Britain has agreed to cede sovereignty of the archipelago, home to the joint U.S.-U.K. Diego Garcia airbase, to Mauritius. A lease arrangement has been worked out to allow continued use of the base, but critics fear a strategic toehold risks falling into the orbit of China.

articles.title: Qatar to present US with new ideas on Iran's Hormuz conditions, Araghchi says
articles.body:
Qatari mediators have agreed to present the United States with fresh ideas developed alongside Tehran to facilitate Iran's conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi announced, indicating that a formal response from Washington could arrive this week.
Speaking to journalists in New York before concluding his diplomatic mission to the United Nations, Araghchi confirmed that he held further discussions with Qatari intermediaries to examine operational paths towards implementing Tehran's requirements.
"They had ideas, and we discussed how a way could be found to meet Iran’s conditions and how those conditions could be fulfilled," Araghchi said, according to the official IRNA news agency.
The diplomatic proposals are now being submitted to US officials, after which Washington's formal position will be transmitted back to Tehran through the intermediary channel.
"I hope this will happen by tomorrow," Araghchi added.
Mediation tracks
Araghchi confirmed that he is departing New York for Tehran within hours, noting that Qatari mediators will convey the American reaction as soon as it is finalised.
The foreign minister highlighted that indirect diplomatic channels conducted through Qatari and Pakistani intermediaries have remained active throughout the crisis, though discussions have grown considerably more focused following Iran's latest seven-day roadmap proposal.
Araghchi reiterated that Tehran actively utilised its bilateral and multilateral engagements in New York to clarify directly to Washington and the wider international community the exact baseline conditions required before commercial shipping can safely resume through the Strait of Hormuz.

articles.title: South Lebanon faces aggressive Israeli offensive as US ‘diplomacy’ provides cover
articles.body:
South Lebanon faces aggressive Israeli offensive as US ‘diplomacy’ provides cover
TEHRAN — A massive explosion orchestrated by Israeli forces tore through the coastal town of al-Mansouri in southern Lebanon on Monday, sending violent tremors across the Tyre district.
Residents miles away felt the ground shake. Based on the pattern of Israel’s offensive conduct, the detonation bore the hallmarks of a calculated demolition designed to erase Lebanese civilian infrastructure and entrench an illegal buffer zone.
Israeli military vehicles later advanced through the fresh ruins to consolidate their positions.
The violence also unfolded across multiple fronts. Israeli warplanes struck the corridor between Mayfadoun and Zawtar al-Sharqiya. An Apache helicopter fired on a commercial center near Mayfadoun twice in ten minutes.
A Merkava tank stationed in Zawtar al-Sharqiyah opened fire on Arnoun. Further inland, the bombardment intensified dramatically.
Artillery units unloaded more than a hundred shells onto Wadi Zebqine in thirty minutes, followed by consecutive air raids on the valley.
Thick smoke choked the sky above Haddatha as heavy machine-gun fire echoed through the hills.
Israel now occupies approximately 600 square kilometers of Lebanese territory stretching up to the Litani River.
Since this phase of Israel’s offensive campaign escalated in March 2026, Lebanon’s Ministry of Public Health has recorded at least 4,386 people killed and 12,407 wounded, pushing the total death toll since October 2023 to 8,953.
Hundreds of thousands of residents remain internally displaced, while entire southern municipalities sit in ruins.
This widespread devastation unfolds under the direct political cover of the United States. While Israeli jets bombed the outskirts of Mays al-Jabal and Tallousa, Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam sat inside the State Department in Washington.
His meeting with Secretary of State Marco Rubio highlighted the glaring hypocrisy of American mediation.
The U.S.-brokered “framework” signed in June promised an immediate ceasefire and a phased Israeli withdrawal. Instead, Washington watched passively as Tel Aviv logged thousands of violations and expanded its military footprint deep into sovereign Lebanese land.
On the ground, the “framework” has bought time for Israel to reshape southern Lebanon by force. Washington continues to arm and shield the Israeli military from international consequences.
Many observers contend that for the Lebanese people enduring daily bombardment, American “diplomacy” has offered nothing but empty rhetoric.

articles.title: Pope Leo XIV urges Russia, Ukraine to sit down at negotiating table
articles.body:
VATICAN CITY, September 29. /TASS/. Pope Leo XIV called on Russia and Ukraine to resolve the conflict at the negotiating table.
"I believe the Church has a responsibility to promote those values, continually inviting leaders such as those of Russia and Ukraine, and other countries, to come, to sit down, to engage in dialogue, to seek ways of resolving problems without continuing these wars that no longer make sense," he said while speaking to journalists from his press pool, which includes a TASS correspondent, on his way back from France.
On September 28, Cardinal Matteo Zuppi, the Pope’s special envoy for Ukraine, arrived in Moscow for the third time. As he told TASS in an interview, his primary mission is to help find solutions to humanitarian issues.
In late August, Vatican Secretary for Relations with States Paul Richard Gallagher visited Moscow.

articles.title: EU Unblocks European Peace Fund for Military Aid to Ukraine
articles.body:
The EU has finally unblocked the European Peace Fund, through which member states are reimbursed for part of the cost of weapons transferred to Ukraine from their own stockpiles.
Kaja Kallas, the EU High Representative for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy, announced this, according to European Pravda.
“The European Peace Fund has also finally been unblocked—and another EUR 1 billion will be allocated for joint arms purchases for Ukraine,” the statement reads.
This refers to the resolution of the issue regarding EUR 6.6 billion.
“There were quite lengthy debates regarding the resolution of the issue concerning EUR 6.6 billion from the European Peace Fund, which had been blocked for quite some time. For the most part, this involves settling past expenditures, but it will also entail the allocation of certain new funds for Ukraine,” it was reported earlier.
The largest portion of the package—EUR 4.7 billion —will go toward compensating member states for the cost of military equipment and weapons they have already transferred to Ukraine.
Another EUR 900 million will fund the EU Mission to Provide Military Assistance to Ukraine, and EUR 1 billion is earmarked for new joint procurements of defense equipment.
Some EU countries have already announced their intention to redirect these funds to support Ukraine once they receive compensation.
In particular, Sweden and Germany have said they will redirect the funds they receive as compensation from the unfrozen European Peace Fund to support Ukraine.
Kaja Kallas also reported that Sweden and Germany are not the only countries willing to redirect the compensation to Ukraine, according to Radio Free Europe.
“Many member states set to receive the funds have already stated that they will transfer them to Ukraine,” Kallas said.
On September 25, EU countries agreed on the terms for releasing EUR 6.6 billion from the European Peace Fund.

articles.title: Bundeswehr Conducted Troop Transfer Drills to NATO’s Eastern Flank in Hamburg
articles.body:
In Hamburg, from September 24 to 26, about 500 Bundeswehr service members, along with police, rescue workers, and civilian companies, practiced redeploying troops, equipment, and cargo to NATO’s eastern flank.
The Bundeswehr reported on this. The Bundeswehr Command conducted the Red Storm Charlie exercise in the state of Hamburg in cooperation with other military units.
According to the exercise scenario, an escalation of the situation on NATO’s eastern flank requires the preemptive deployment of additional forces to strengthen deterrence.
Troops and their equipment arrive in Hamburg and then continue eastward. Part of the route passes through the city itself.
“Just like last year during Red Storm Bravo, in Red Storm Charlie we are practicing the redeployment of troops and equipment to the Alliance’s eastern flank,” Captain 1st Class Kurt Leonard, commander of the Bundeswehr Command in Hamburg, shared.
Most movements took place at night to minimize the exercises’ impact on traffic and city operations.
Helicopters were also involved in the exercises, used to escort and monitor the movement of military convoys from the air.
One of the main objectives of Red Storm Charlie was the interaction between the military and civilian services and businesses that could be called upon to support the country’s defense.
The fire department, the Hamburg police, the Federal Office for Technical Relief, and local authorities trained alongside the Bundeswehr.
Civilian companies and critical infrastructure operators also joined the exercises, including Airbus, the port and logistics company HHLA, and the Hamburg Port Authority.
Participants practiced joint operations as troops, equipment, and cargo moved through the port and urban infrastructure.
The Bundeswehr emphasizes that the country’s defense and infrastructure resilience depend not only on the military.
“Defense and resilience are tasks for society as a whole, which the Bundeswehr cannot accomplish on its own,” Kurt Leonards noted.
The exercises are part of preparations for implementing Germany’s Operational Plan, which outlines coordination among the military, government agencies, and the civilian sector during the country’s defense and the fulfillment of allied obligations.
One of the plan’s key objectives is to ensure German territory is used as a logistics hub for moving allied troops and cargo toward NATO’s eastern flank.
Red Storm Charlie follows on from last year’s Red Storm Bravo exercises. This year, the organizers have expanded the range of participants and placed greater emphasis on cooperation between the military and civilian structures.
In total, the exercises involved about 500 military personnel, along with numerous vehicles and helicopters. Representatives of civilian organizations are also participating separately, bringing their own equipment and machinery.
